title: Databases
oneLiner: Pick by data shape, then: Multi-AZ survives failure, read replicas scale reads, Aurora Global covers regions. Cache with lazy loading or write-through plus TTL. DynamoDB on-demand is the default now.

notes.html: Pick by data shape first: tables with joins, key-value at any scale, documents, graph, time series. Then pick for HA and reads.

head: Trigger
Answer
Why / do instead
rows: Aurora for more performance, 15 replicas, global
Key-value, any scale, serverless, single-digit ms
Not for ad-hoc joins or complex queries
QLDB reached end of support in July 2025; older questions still say QLDB

notes.html: One rule: Multi-AZ is for surviving failure, read replicas are for reads. Multi-AZ copies synchronously and fails over by itself; replicas copy asynchronously and you promote them by hand.

notes.caption: Sync for HA, async for reads and DR

head: Multi-AZ (instance)
Read replica
Cross-region replica
rows: You pay for the standby (about 2× instance cost)

items: A Multi-AZ DB cluster (newer RDS option) has two readable standbys. The classic Multi-AZ instance standby is not readable.
Up to 15 read replicas, and a replica can itself be Multi-AZ.
Automated backups keep up to 35 days and can replicate to another region. Longer → manual snapshots or AWS Backup.
Multi-AZ DB cluster (or a read replica)

questions.q: An RDS MySQL instance was created unencrypted. Compliance now requires encryption at rest. What works?

options.t: Take a snapshot, copy it with encryption using a KMS key, restore a new instance from the copy, and switch the app
options.why: The only path: encryption can't be turned on in place.

options.t: Modify the instance and enable encryption
options.why: RDS doesn't allow enabling encryption on an existing instance.

options.t: Create an encrypted read replica and promote it
options.why: An unencrypted primary can't have an encrypted replica.

options.t: Enable default EBS encryption for the account
options.why: Affects new EBS volumes, not RDS storage that already exists.

questions.q: A team must encrypt an existing unencrypted Aurora cluster with the least data loss and a short cutover. Which plan fits?

options.t: Snapshot the cluster, restore it as a new cluster with encryption on, then cut over in a short write freeze
options.why: Restore is the encryption path; freezing writes during the switch avoids loss.

options.t: Turn on encryption in the cluster settings during the maintenance window
options.why: Not possible for an existing cluster.

options.t: Add an encrypted Aurora replica to the cluster
options.why: Replicas share the cluster's storage and encryption setting.

options.t: Encrypt the data in the application and leave storage as is
options.why: Doesn't meet encryption at rest for the database, and is a big app change.

questions.q: A production RDS PostgreSQL database must keep running with minimal downtime if its AZ fails, with no manual steps.

options.t: Enable Multi-AZ
options.why: Synchronous standby in another AZ with automatic failover.

options.t: Add a read replica in another AZ
options.why: Async, and you have to promote it yourself.

options.t: Take hourly snapshots
options.why: Restoring takes time and loses up to an hour.

options.t: Add a cross-region read replica
options.why: For DR across regions; still a manual promote.

questions.q: Monthly reports slow down an RDS MySQL primary. The fix must need the least change and not slow writes.

options.t: Create a read replica and point the reporting tool at its endpoint
options.why: Offloads reads; async so writes aren't slowed.

options.t: Enable Multi-AZ and read from the standby
options.why: A Multi-AZ instance standby isn't readable.

options.t: Put ElastiCache in front of the reports
options.why: Ad-hoc reports rarely repeat the same query; a cache helps little.

options.t: Move the database to DynamoDB
options.why: Huge change, and reports need SQL.

questions.q: An RDS MySQL app needs disaster recovery in another region with an RPO of a few minutes, at the lowest cost without migrating engines.

options.t: A cross-region read replica, promoted during a disaster
options.why: Async copy with minutes of lag; you only pay for one replica.

options.t: Enable Multi-AZ
options.why: Single region only.

options.t: Daily snapshots copied to the other region
options.why: RPO up to 24 hours.

options.t: Migrate to Aurora Global Database
options.why: Better RPO, but a migration and a higher cost than needed.

questions.q: Finance asks what enabling Multi-AZ on an RDS instance does to the bill. What's correct?

options.t: You pay for the standby instance too, so instance cost roughly doubles; the sync traffic inside the region is free
options.why: The standby is a full instance you pay for.

options.t: Nothing changes: the standby is free
options.why: The standby is billed.

options.t: Only storage doubles, the standby compute is free
options.why: Both are billed.

options.t: You pay only when a failover happens
options.why: It's billed all the time.

questions.q: A global trading app needs a relational database with reads in three regions, RPO about 1 second and RTO about 1 minute if the primary region fails.

options.t: Aurora Global Database
options.why: Storage-level replication under a second, and a secondary can be promoted in about a minute.

options.t: RDS Multi-AZ
options.why: One region.

options.t: RDS cross-region read replicas
options.why: Async with more lag, and slower to promote.

options.t: DynamoDB Global Tables
options.why: Not relational.

questions.q: An internal app's database is idle most of the day with unpredictable bursts. The team wants a relational DB that minimizes cost and scales without dropping connections.

options.t: Aurora Serverless v2
options.why: Scales capacity in seconds and you pay for what you use.

options.t: Aurora Serverless v1
options.why: Retired, and it scaled slowly with pauses.

options.t: A large provisioned RDS instance
options.why: Paying for peak all day.

options.t: RDS with Storage Auto Scaling
options.why: Grows storage, not compute.

questions.q: Hundreds of concurrent Lambda invocations exhaust connections on an RDS PostgreSQL database. What's the least effort fix?

options.t: Put RDS Proxy between Lambda and the database
options.why: Pools and reuses connections.

options.t: Increase max_connections and the instance size
options.why: Bigger bill, and the next spike breaks it again.

options.t: Add a read replica
options.why: Doesn't help write connections, and Lambda still opens many.

options.t: Set Lambda reserved concurrency to 1
options.why: Fixes connections by throttling the app.

questions.q: A security team wants apps on EC2 to connect to RDS MySQL with no stored database password at all.

options.t: IAM database authentication with short-lived auth tokens
options.why: The instance role gets a token; there's no password to store or rotate.

options.t: Store the password in Secrets Manager with rotation
options.why: Still a password, just better managed.

options.t: Put the password in user data
options.why: Stored in plain text in instance metadata.

options.t: Use a security group rule instead of a password
options.why: Network control, not authentication.

questions.q: An RDS database keeps running out of disk space during unpredictable growth. Ops wants it handled with no manual intervention.

options.t: Enable RDS Storage Auto Scaling with a maximum size
options.why: Grows storage automatically with no downtime.

options.t: Create a CloudWatch alarm that emails the DBA
options.why: Still manual.

options.t: Move to Aurora Serverless v1
options.why: Retired, and a migration for a storage problem.

options.t: Add a read replica
options.why: Replicas don't add storage to the primary.

questions.q: A product catalog is read heavily, and users must never see stale prices from the cache. Which caching strategy fits?

options.t: Write-through: update the cache whenever the database is written
options.why: The cache always matches the DB.

options.t: Lazy loading with no TTL
options.why: Entries can stay stale until evicted.

options.t: Session store
options.why: That's a use case, not a caching strategy.

options.t: Cache only on a miss, with a 24-hour TTL
options.why: Up to a day of stale prices.

questions.q: An app uses lazy loading. Some users see data that's hours old. The team wants to keep lazy loading but limit staleness.

options.t: Add a TTL to cache entries
options.why: Entries expire and are reloaded on the next miss.

options.t: Switch the cache to Memcached
options.why: Engine choice doesn't change staleness.

options.t: Use session store as the strategy
options.why: Not a caching strategy.

options.t: Add more cache nodes
options.why: More capacity, same staleness.

questions.q: A web tier behind an ALB must be stateless so any instance can fail without logging users out.

options.t: Store sessions in ElastiCache (or DynamoDB) with a TTL
options.why: Shared, fast session data outside the instances.

options.t: Turn on ALB sticky sessions
options.why: Sessions die with the instance.

options.t: Store sessions on instance store
options.why: Lost if the instance fails.

options.t: Store sessions on each instance's EBS volume
options.why: Still tied to one instance.

questions.q: A new mobile app's DynamoDB traffic is unknown and spiky. The team wants the least capacity management at a reasonable cost.

options.t: On-demand capacity mode
options.why: Scales per request; AWS now recommends it by default after the 2024 price cut.

options.t: Provisioned mode with fixed RCU/WCU
options.why: Throttles on spikes, overpays when quiet.

options.t: Provisioned with auto scaling, since on-demand costs 2.5× per request
options.why: That ratio is outdated; on-demand fell about 50% in Nov 2024, and auto scaling lags spikes.

options.t: Add DAX
options.why: A cache, not a capacity mode.

questions.q: A DynamoDB table serves a steady, predictable load near the same level 24/7. What's the most cost-effective mode?

options.t: Provisioned capacity, with reserved capacity for the baseline
options.why: High, steady utilization is where provisioned still wins.

options.t: On-demand
options.why: Simpler, but costs more at steady high use.

options.t: On-demand with DAX
options.why: DAX adds cost; doesn't change the mode math.

options.t: Global Tables
options.why: Multi-region replication, not a pricing mode.

questions.q: An app does 10 strongly consistent reads per second of 6 KB items. How many RCUs?

options.why: 6 KB rounds up to 8 KB = 2 RCU per read; 10 × 2 = 20.
Each read needs 2 units because 6 KB is more than 4 KB.
Item size rounds up to the next 4 KB, not 1.5 units.
That rounds to 12 KB; rounding is to the next 4 KB.

questions.q: A read-heavy DynamoDB app needs microsecond read latency with no application code rewrite.

options.t: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)
options.why: A drop-in cache that speaks the DynamoDB API.

options.t: ElastiCache for Redis
options.why: Fast, but the app must add cache logic.

options.t: DynamoDB Global Tables
options.why: For multi-region, not latency inside one region.

options.t: Switch to on-demand mode
options.why: Billing mode, not latency.

questions.q: A MongoDB-compatible app on DocumentDB needs DR in a second region with low RPO and minimal operational overhead.

options.t: DocumentDB Global Clusters
options.why: Managed cross-region replication with fast promotion.

options.t: DocumentDB is single-region, so rewrite for DynamoDB Global Tables
options.why: Global Clusters exist; no rewrite needed.

options.t: Self-managed MongoDB replica sets on EC2
options.why: Lots of operations work.

options.t: Copy snapshots to the other region nightly
options.why: RPO up to a day.

questions.q: A team is designing a new system that needs a tamper-evident history of every change. Someone suggests QLDB. What's correct?

options.t: QLDB reached end of support in July 2025; build on Aurora PostgreSQL. Older exam questions may still expect QLDB
options.why: AWS's migration path is Aurora PostgreSQL.

options.t: QLDB is the current AWS answer for any ledger
options.why: It's retired.

options.t: Use DynamoDB with versioning turned on
options.why: DynamoDB has no item versioning feature.

options.t: Use S3 Standard with lifecycle rules
options.why: Lifecycle moves data; it doesn't prove history.
